models.name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B
models.description: Qwen3 Coder 30B MoE - Code-specialized (3B active params). Best for code generation. 256K native context.
notes: MoE model: only 3B params active per token — very fast on 128GB unified memory
n_threads=4 is optimal for MoE: CPU handles expert routing, fewer threads = less contention
cache_type_k/v q8_0: halves KV memory cost, negligible quality loss, enables large context
no_context_shift: prevents early prompt tokens (function signatures etc.) being rotated out
n_predict=-1: let EOS stop generation naturally — critical for code gen
jinja=true: required for correct chat template and tool calling
Official Qwen params: temp=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, repeat_penalty=1.05

models.name: Gemma-4-31B
models.description: Gemma 4 31B Dense - Reasoning, coding, multimodal (256K context). Google's flagship open model.
notes: DENSE model (not MoE): all 31B params active every token — heavier than Qwen3 MoE
CRITICAL: flash_attn MUST be false — known bug causes infinite hang on prompts >3-4K tokens with FA enabled on Dense 31B
repeat_penalty=1.0: Google explicitly says Gemma 4 does NOT require repeat penalty by default; 1.15 hurts quality
temperature=0.7: Lowered from official 1.0 to reduce very long responses (1.0 causes endless generation)
top_k=64: Google's official value for Gemma 4
THINKING MODE: Controlled via prompt-level enable_thinking parameter (in promptConfig.json, not here)
Gemma-4 generates <|channel>thought\n<channel|> tags by default. Set enable_thinking=false in prompt to minimize overhead
cache_type_k/v q8_0: safe to use even without flash_attn
ctx_size=32768: conservative given no flash_attn; increase to 65536 only if prompts stay short
n_predict=512: Prevents endless thinking chains while allowing reasonable response length

models.name: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B
models.description: Qwen3 Vision Language 30B MoE - Multimodal text+image (256K native). Requires mmproj file.
notes: MoE model: 3B active params, same as Coder variant — n_threads=4 optimal
Q2_K is heavily quantized: 131072 ctx in original config is unrealistic — will OOM
REQUIRES mmproj file: update mmproj path to your actual mmproj-F16.gguf location
flash_attn=true: safe for VL MoE variant unlike the Gemma 4 Dense issue
Follow standard Qwen3 sampling: temp=0.7, top_k=20, top_p=0.8
Place image content BEFORE text in multimodal prompts for best results
ctx_size=32768: realistic ceiling for Q2_K quant on this model

models.name: GLM-4.6V-Flash
models.description: GLM 4.6 Vision Flash - Multi-modal reasoning, optimized speed. Requires external Jinja template.
notes: CRITICAL: chat_template_file is mandatory — GLM Jinja templates have known llama-server compatibility issues
Extract template: huggingface-cli download THUDM/glm-4v-flash tokenizer_config.json then extract chat_template key to .jinja file
repeat_penalty=1.0: looping in GLM is caused by wrong template, NOT insufficient penalty — fixing template makes 1.0 correct
ctx_size=32768: 65536 is wasteful for a Q8 vision model; 32768 is practical
mmproj: update path to actual mmproj-GLM-4.6V-Flash-Q8_0.gguf location
flash_attn=true: GLM 4.6 supports FA without the Gemma 4 Dense bug
If still getting garbage output after template fix: verify with --verbose that chat_format shows custom not Content-only

models.name: LFM2-24B-A2B
models.description: LFM2 24B active - Liquid AI hybrid SSM+attention model. General purpose. (⚠️ Q4_0 = lower quality, consider Q4_K_M upgrade)
notes: Hybrid SSM+attention architecture (not pure transformer) — unique inference characteristics
Q4_0 is the lowest quality quant: consider upgrading to Q4_K_M or Q5_K_M from LiquidAI/LFM2-24B-A2B-GGUF
REQUIRES chat_template_file: download from https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2-24B-A2B/blob/main/chat_template.jinja
generation_config.json has NO sampling params — LiquidAI intentionally leaves tuning to user
EOS token ID=7, BOS token ID=1 — verify these are baked correctly in GGUF with gguf-dump
stop_type must be 'eos' not 'limit' — if you see 'limit' the template is not loading correctly
temperature=0.1 kept from original: LFM2 is a more deterministic model by nature
MoE model: n_threads=4 optimal same as Qwen3 MoE variants

models.name: Qwen3.5-9B
models.description: Qwen 3.5 9B - Fast, lightweight, high quality at small size (262K native context). Best for quick tasks.
notes: Dense 9B model: fast on your 128GB unified memory — good for quick Q&A and short tasks
temperature=0.7 corrected from 1.0: 1.0 is too creative/random for a utility model
Q5_K_M is a good quant for 9B: high quality with reasonable memory footprint (~6GB)
ctx_size=65536: realistic for 9B Q5_K_M on 128GB unified memory
n_threads=8: dense model benefits from more CPU threads than MoE variants
flash_attn=true: safe and beneficial for this dense model
cache_type_k/v q8_0: safe quality/memory tradeoff
Note: Qwen3.5 mmproj vision files are separate — if you need vision use Qwen3-VL instead
n_predict=-1: let EOS stop naturally

models.name: SmolVLM-500M
models.description: SmolVLM 500M - Tiny vision-language model for image understanding. SOTA for memory footprint (820MB F16).
notes: TINY VLM: only 500M params — extremely fast, low RAM (~1.5GB with image), perfect for edge/mobile deployment
REQUIRES mmproj file: update path to your mmproj-model-f16.gguf from ggml-org/SmolVLM-500M-Instruct-GGUF
F16 CRITICAL for quality: quantization (Q8/Q4) severely hurts quality on models this small — always use F16
Context: 8192 native — encodes each 384x384 patch to only 81 tokens (vs 16K for Qwen2-VL), very efficient
Best for: image captioning, visual Q&A, OCR, document understanding, quick vision tasks
Image placement: <image> tag should be at START of prompt for best results per llama.cpp testing
temperature=0.8: balanced for creative visual descriptions without hallucination (no official recommendation)
top_p=0.95, top_k=40: standard VLM sampling — small model needs wider search space
repeat_penalty=1.0: instruction-tuned model doesn't need penalty (follow Gemma 4 pattern)
n_threads=12: small dense model, benefits from parallelism but not as heavy as 9B+
flash_attn=true: safe for SmolVLM — confirmed working in llama.cpp PR #13050
Architecture: Idefics3-based, uses SmolLM2-360M text decoder + SigLIP-93M vision encoder
ctx_size=8192: use full native context — model can handle multiple images efficiently
Download: ggml-org/SmolVLM-500M-Instruct-GGUF on HuggingFace (820MB f16 text + 190MB f16 mmproj)

models.name: Qwen3.5-27B
models.description: Qwen 3.5 27B - Dense flagship model with hybrid Gated DeltaNet+Attention. Reasoning, coding, multilingual (262K native context). Q5_K_M quantization.
notes: DENSE 27B: all params active every token — heavier than Qwen3.5-9B, use for complex reasoning/coding tasks
Official: Qwen3.5 operates in thinking mode by default — generates thinking content before final response
Hybrid Gated DeltaNet+Gated Attention architecture: NOT standard MHA — provides efficient scaling
Context: 262,144 tokens native, extensible to 1,010,000 with YaRN RoPE scaling
Q5_K_M quantization: ~17-18GB for 27B, good balance of quality and speed (vs F16 ~51GB)
Official sampling params (Instruct/non-thinking mode): temp=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, min_p=0.0, repeat_penalty=1.0
Thinking mode (general): temp=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, presence_penalty=1.5 — enables extended reasoning
Coding mode (thinking): temp=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, presence_penalty=0.0 — more deterministic for code
n_threads=16: dense model with all 27B params active benefits from higher parallelism than MoE variants
flash_attn=true: safe and benefits hybrid architecture; gating mechanisms optimize memory
cache_type_k/v q8_0: standard compaction, safe for quality on reasoning model
n_predict=-1: let EOS stop naturally, model learned proper stopping behavior
ctx_size=65536: conservative for Q5_K_M on 128GB unified memory; can scale to 128K+ if needed
Disable thinking: pass chat_template_kwargs={enable_thinking: False} at inference for instruct-only mode
Min output length recommended: 32,768 tokens for general queries, 81,920 for complex math/coding
No jinja/template file needed: native support via pretrained chat template

models.name: Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q5_K_M
models.description: Qwen3 Coder Next 80B MoE (3B active) - Agentic coding with long-horizon reasoning, tool-calling, and execution recovery. Fast code generation with 256K native context.
notes: MoE MODEL: 80B total params / 3B active per token — extremely fast, comparable to 10-20× larger dense models
Hybrid architecture: 12 layers with Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention + 512 experts (10 activated) per layer
NON-THINKING mode only: no <think></think> blocks — ultra-fast agentic responses without reasoning overhead
Expert routing: n_threads=4 optimal (same as Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B) — CPU handles routing, fewer threads = less contention
Qwen-recommended sampling (OFFICIAL from Hugging Face & Unsloth docs): temp=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=40, min_p=0.01, repeat_penalty=disabled/1.0
repeat_penalty=1.0: Unsloth confirms 'disabled or 1.0' — llama-server defaults to 1.05, override to 1.0 if looping observed
min_p=0.01: Unsloth explicitly sets 0.01 (vs llama-server default 0.05) — important for tool calling quality
Context: 262,144 tokens native — can set to 32,768 for less memory use if prompts are small
Q5_K_M quant: ~55-59GB estimated (check Unsloth repo for exact size) — balance of quality and speed
Tool-calling: ENABLED by default — excels at long-horizon reasoning, function calls, recovery from failures
cache_type_k/v q8_0: safe for KV compaction; halves memory cost with negligible quality loss
flash_attn=true: safe and beneficial for MoE routing efficiency
jinja=true: required for correct chat template and tool calling support
n_predict=-1: let EOS stop naturally — model trained for proper stopping behavior
IMPORTANT: Feb 4 llama.cpp fix corrected vectorized key_gdiff calculation — must use latest llama.cpp (>b8665)
If model loops/poor output: ensure llama.cpp is updated AND repeat_penalty is not >1.1
Feb 19 update: Tool-calling improved after llama.cpp parsing fixes

_meta.hardware: GMKTec EVO X2 — AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S (40CU RDNA 3.5), 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 unified memory
_meta.recommended_llama_server_build: Vulkan (llama-bXXXX-bin-win-vulkan-x64) — HIP/ROCm builds result in GPU being unused on Windows due to KV cache dumping to shared memory on Strix Halo gfx1151
_meta.vulkan_backend_advantage: RADV Vulkan beats HIP on Strix Halo for both prompt processing and token generation. MoE models show largest gains.
_meta.global_flags_to_add_in_launch_code: --jinja must be passed as CLI flag regardless of model. chat_template_file and mmproj are also CLI flags not JSON fields — your launch code must map these from the JSON to actual CLI arguments.
